what: Sempra owns regulated utilities in California and Texas, plus liquefied natural gas export terminals. In California it owns San Diego Gas and Electric and SoCalGas; in Texas it owns most of Oncor, the state's largest electricity delivery network.
customers: Californian and Texan households and businesses through its utilities, and international buyers of liquefied natural gas.
money: SDG&E electricity and SoCalGas gas distribution
LNG export terminals and Mexican energy infrastructure
moat: Regulated networks in two of the fastest-growing US states, plus LNG export capacity that is sold out under long-term contracts.
risks: Debt of about $35 billion against under $1 billion of cash
California wildfire liability is a persistent risk for utilities there
LNG projects are very large and exposed to cost overruns
Mexican infrastructure assets carry political risk
opportunities: Texas electricity demand is growing faster than anywhere in the country, which drives Oncor's investment
Analysts see about 25% upside to the current price
LNG exports under long-term contracts add earnings outside the regulated business
watch: Oncor capital spending approvals and LNG project construction progress.
